title: Autocraft: admin utility orchestrator for idempotent support microflows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight orchestrator (Autocraft) that converts curated runbook steps into idempotent, auditable microflows usable by support engineers and automated remediation systems. Focus is on safe dry-run and sandbox execution, policy-enforced fallbacks, and compact observability exposed to Console for per-step latency/cost breakdowns.
acceptance_criteria: Autocraft can import a YAML runbook bundle and synthesize a task graph inside the admin-agent sandbox
Each step must be idempotent or annotated with compensation logic; executor enforces idempotency token semantics
Dry-run mode must produce a replayable plan and a telemetry trace viewable in Console (per-step timing and token counts)
Rollout guardrails: canary execution on 10% of incidents, automatic rollback on >2 failing steps within 5 minutes
Audit logs for each execution stored in encrypted S3 path and surfaced to the audit UI with KMS key metadata
tasks: Spike: prototype YAML->task-graph translator (done, prototype branch autocraft/spike-yaml)
Design: finalize step contract (inputs, outputs, idempotency, compensation) and publish Confluence spec
Implement: executor v1 in Go as a lightweight binary alongside admin-agent
Integrate: telemetry hook that emits per-step events to tracing + cost metrics pipeline
QA: dry-run harness and simulated incident replay for oncall training
Docs: quickstart, CLI examples, and Console panel wireframes

decisions: Implement executor in Go for binary size, observability integration, and easier cgroups/ptrace safety controls
Task graph model chosen over imperative script approach to enable fine-grained telemetry, step retry policies, and deterministic dry-run
Idempotency model: each step must accept an op_id; server will persist step results keyed by op_id to prevent duplicate effects
Audit storage will use S3 with KMS envelope keys; CloudTrail-style index written to Postgres for quick lookup in Console
blockers: KMS key provisioning for staging account (security ticket SEC-2025-115)
Quota for sandboxed GPU hosts when trying full dry-run against real models — infra needs temporary burst (ENG-677001)
Small design question: whether compensation logic should be optional or enforced for all mutating steps
